hints.text: Substituting gives $\frac{0}{0}$, which is a signal — not an answer. Factor the top.
$x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3)$, so the $(x - 3)$ on top cancels the one on the bottom.
What is left is $x + 3$, and at $x = 3$ that is $6$.

explanation: Substituting $x = 3$ gives $\frac{0}{0}$, which means more work is needed, not that there is no answer.
Factor the top as a difference of squares: $x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3)$.
Cancel the shared factor $(x - 3)$, which leaves $x + 3$ everywhere except at the hole.
Now substituting is safe: $3 + 3 = 6$, so the limit is $6$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sneak up with a table
steps: Try an input just below $3$: at $x = 2.9$ the fraction is $\frac{8.41 - 9}{-0.1} = 5.9$, and at $x = 2.99$ it is $5.99$.
Try an input just above $3$: at $x = 3.1$ the fraction is $\frac{9.61 - 9}{0.1} = 6.1$, and at $x = 3.01$ it is $6.01$.
Both sides squeeze toward the same number, so the limit is $6$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Look at the graph
steps: Away from $x = 3$ the fraction equals $x + 3$, so its graph is the straight line $y = x + 3$.
The only difference is one open circle at $x = 3$, where the original fraction is undefined.
The line passes through height $3 + 3 = 6$ at that spot, so the graph heads to $6$ and the limit is $6$.
